review_mode: Read-only mathematical statement and scope review; recorded author compile/audit receipts checked without running Lean. Only this review report was written.

scope.codec_domain: Infinite signed integer arrays indexed by natural coordinates.
scope.finite_digits: Fin(a-1) -> Fin(b-1) -> Fin k, extended to an infinite prefix-offset array by zero outside the interior rectangle.
scope.cardinality: The constructed finite-digit encoded image for a fixed infinite original array has k^((a-1)(b-1)) distinct members. This is not the full accepted finite-table fiber theorem.
scope.margin_statements: Explicit finite range sums, under full zero prefix boundary or divisible-margin conditions. Finite-table extension and restriction adapters remain outstanding.
scope.physical_margins: Actual positive physical states with the source capacity and reference row/column Option types; fine margin definitions use d=the full ambient dimensionAllowance.

validated_points: difference uses adjacent mixed differences; prefixSum is exactly the northwest finite range sum. difference_prefix holds for arbitrary signed arrays, while prefix_difference needs only ZeroAxes.

BoundedDigits requires every digit to lie in [0,k); positive k gives Euclidean floor quotient and nonnegative remainder, including negative prefix numerators. scaled_digit_ediv and scaled_digit_emod have the correct quantifiers.

decode_encode requires positive k, ZeroAxes, and BoundedDigits. residue_encode has no separate positive-k hypothesis because its bounded-digit assumptions already force positive k. encode_decode is the signed division-with-remainder identity and legitimately holds even without positivity.
codecEquiv is an equivalence between Array times infinite offset arrays and Array. The documentation explicitly denies any finite cardinality inference from this equivalence.

difference_bounds has both lower and upper bounds with the correct integer k-1 endpoints. encode_entry_at_least_two uses nonnegativity of the original entry and positive k; accepted_fine_entry_at_least_two uses decode nonnegativity without demanding that an arbitrary fine array be feasible.
ZeroBoundary a b imposes zeros on the entire top and left axes and on the entire row a and column b. This is stronger than saying only finitely many boundary points vanish and is accurately stated.

encode_row_margin and encode_column_margin sum exactly b or a entries and produce k*(old margin+2b) and k*(old margin+2a). Zero-width rectangles use natural subtraction and range-empty conventions consistently.

residue_zero_boundary_of_divisible_margins assumes divisible finite-width row sums for every natural row and divisible finite-height column sums for every natural column. A finite-table adapter must provide an outside extension satisfying these global hypotheses.

decode_row_margin and decode_column_margin use a nonzero k and the recovered zero boundary. They do not silently assume floor(sum/k)=sum(floor/k). The formulas are derived through the exact encode_decode identity.
finiteOffsets restricts digits to 0<p<a and 0<q<b and is zero everywhere else. Therefore it supplies the full zero boundary and global bounded-digit condition for positive k.

FiniteDigits cardinality and finiteEncode injectivity justify encodedFamily_card on Set.range in the infinite-array codomain. Restriction injectivity and whole finite-fiber surjectivity are not stated or certified.

Outside extensions matter: encoding a zero-extended original finite table yields 2k outside the rectangle, whereas decoding a zero-extended fine table yields -2 outside. Equality of two differently zero-extended arrays cannot be inferred from equality of their finite restrictions.

A suitable eventual adapter may extend the original finite table by zero and the fine table by 2k, or may work with restricted equality throughout. The final source comments explicitly preserve this distinction.
